title: ALMA view of the circumstellar environment of the post-common-envelope-evolution binary system HD 101584
question: What are the morphology, kinematics, masses and energetics of the circumstellar environment of the post-AGB binary HD 101584, and does it match common-envelope scenarios?

evidence.quote: The single-dish 12 CO(2–1) flux is 850 Jy km s [−][1] (Olofsson & Nyman 1999)

what.value: SED model and dust temperature 45 K, mass 0.6 Msun, distance 0.7 kpc

evidence.quote: an adopted dust temperature of 45 K [from the SED in Bakker et al. (1996b)]
the dust opacity κ 230 = 0.5 cm [2] g [−][1] (Liseau et al. 2015)

what.value: Orbital period 218 d and K1 = 3 km/s

evidence.quote: Adopting the orbital parameters (period _P_ = 218 days and velocity semi-amplitude _K_ 1 = 3 km s [−][1] )

what.value: Rotational temperature 30 K; proto-PN energy and momentum ranges

recipe.goal: Measure continuum and global line fluxes
recipe.method: Continuum map from line-free bandwidth; line fluxes integrated over global profiles; compared with SED and SEST

recipe.goal: Morphology and kinematics from channel maps and PV diagram
recipe.method: Velocity-channel maps and PV diagram along PA=90 deg; age from projected length and velocity with tilt 10 deg
assumptions: Inclination about half the hour-glass opening angle, ≈ 10 deg

recipe.method: Dust mass from the 1.3 mm flux (Eq. 1); gas mass from C18O(2-1) (Eq. 2)
assumptions: D = 0.7 kpc, kappa230 = 0.5 cm2/g, Td = 45 K, dust-to-gas 200

recipe.goal: Energetics and comparison with orbital energy
recipe.method: Kinetic energy and momentum of gas at ≥10 km/s from C18O; orbital mass function and released orbital energy for the capture scenario
assumptions: circular orbit, i=10 deg, M1=0.6 Msun, M1,i=1.6 Msun, a2,i=4 AU

answer_key.uncertainty: at least a factor of four

evidence.quote: is ≈ 4 × 10 [45] erg (a lower limit since extended flux from accelerated gas is missed)

evidence.loc: 3.2 A jet, an hour-glass structure, and the central region
evidence.quote: the age is estimated to be ≈ 500 yr.
we estimate that _M_ 2 ≈ 0.6 _M_ ⊙ at a distance of _a_ ≈ 0.7 AU
